name: ABeta Amyloidosis, Italian Type
aliases: ABeta Amyloidosis of the Italian Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for ABeta Amyloidosis, Italian Type

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of amyloid deposits with Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence
Identification of ABeta amyloid fibrils by immunohistochemistry or mass spectrometry
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Presence of progressive neurological symptoms including cognitive decline and ataxia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation of amyloid deposits with ABeta peptide identification plus compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not definitive due to heterogeneity.

laboratory: Congo red staining positive for amyloid deposits in biopsy specimens
Immunohistochemical detection of ABeta peptide in affected tissues
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tau protein and decreased amyloid-beta 42 levels
imaging: MRI showing cerebral microbleeds and white matter hyperintensities
Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) revealing cerebral amyloid angiopathy
PET amyloid imaging positive for ABeta deposits
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Progressive neurological decline despite supportive care

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of widespread neurofibrillary tangles and plaques rather than vascular amyloid deposits
More prominent memory impairment early in disease course
Lack of recurrent intracerebral hemorrhages typical of cerebral amyloid angiopathy
Amyloid deposits composed of transthyretin rather than ABeta peptide
Different genetic mutations in TTR gene

redFlags: Recurrent lobar intracerebral hemorrhages in middle-aged adults
Rapidly progressive dementia with cerebellar signs
Family history of similar neurological symptoms with autosomal dominant pattern
references: Orphanet: ABeta Amyloidosis, Italian Type - ORPHA:324713
Campion D, et al. Familial British and Danish dementia: clinical and genetic features. Brain. 1999.
Maat-Schieman ML, et al. ABeta amyloidosis in familial British dementia. Acta Neuropathol. 2000.
